title: An east-west Pacific temperature contrast gave no clear six-month ENSO forecast gain in 1981-2024
abstract: We tested whether Nino 3 minus Nino 4 temperature anomalies improve six-month Nino 3.4 forecasts after season, recent temperature change and separate warm and cold slopes are included. We used a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 snapshot and 528 monthly origins in 1981-2024. Annual expanding fits used only completed earlier targets. The added contrast raised mean squared error by 0.81%. The conditional 95% five-year block interval for error reduction was -9.49% to +8.17%. RMSE rose from 0.685841 to 0.688601 C. Rolling training, a time trend, removal of the absolute-temperature term and other lead times left gains uncertain. The test gives no clear added gain under these models. It does not establish that spatial information has no value. Revised records, few independent cycles, overlapping prior campaign studies and conditional uncertainty limit inference. Original code, aggregate scores, source hashes, numerical checks and a figure support reproduction. Source records and individual prediction rows remain external.

display.caption: MSE reductions with conditional 95% five-year block limits, and cumulative annual mean saved loss. Positive values favor the contrast model.
